screening_decisions.reason: Multicentre RCT evaluating adjuvant medroxyprogesterone acetate (progestagen) after surgery for endometrial cancer. Meets all criteria (RCT, progestagen, women who had surgery).
This is a narrative review of clinical observations, not a randomised controlled trial. Does not satisfy the study design requirement.
The paper discusses a methodological quantity (I²) for meta-analyses; it is not a clinical trial of progestagen therapy in endometrial cancer.
This is a book chapter on statistical methods for meta-analysis, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Large RCT (n=1148) of adjuvant progestagen (progesterone) after surgery for stage I/II endometrial cancer. Clearly meets all selection criteria.
Methodological paper on random-effects meta-analysis; not an RCT of progestagen therapy.

Randomised trial of progestogen as part of primary treatment, which included surgery (all patients >1 year post-operation). The therapy was given in conjunction with surgery and radiotherapy. Although labelled 'primary treatment', the patients had surgery and received progestogen; conservative inclusion is appropriate.
Methodological paper on extracting log hazard ratios for meta-analysis; not a randomised trial of progestagen therapy.
Small randomised placebo-controlled trial (n=35) of adjuvant 6-methyl-17α-hydroxyprogesterone after hysterectomy for stage I endometrial cancer. Meets criteria, though small sample size.
Prospective RCT (n=205) of adjuvant progestagen after hysterectomy for endometrial cancer. The random assignment and comparison of progestagen vs. no additional therapy satisfy the criteria.
